sections.overview: Trikantaka Ghrita – Benefits, Usage, Indications and Dosage
sections.introduction: Trikantaka Ghrita is an Ayurvedic formulation with clarified butter as its base. It is basically used to cure urinary and renal disorders.
sections.ingredients:
Trikantaka (Tribulus terrestris] 
 Water for decoction – 12.288 liters boiled and reduced to 3.072 liters 

 9.140 grams of each of:- 

 Cardamom (Elettaria cardamomum) 
 Shilajit (Asphaltum) 
 Shilabheda (Aerva lanata) 
 Licorice (Glycyrrhiza glabra) 
 Shatavari (Asparagus racemosus) 
 Darbha (Desmostachya bipinnata) 
 Ambu (Pavonia odorata) 
 Shaundi (Piper longum) 
 Vasuka (Adhatoda zeylanica) 
 Vasiraka (Piper cubeba) 
 Kasha (Saccharum spontaneum) 
 Ikshumoola (Root of sugarcane) 
 Matsyakshika (Enhydra fluctuans) 
 Milk 
 Ghee / Clarified butter 

 Method of Preparation 
 Combine the mentioned herbs and decoction and add them to the clarified butter. Heat them till the herbs are completely infused in it and the clarified butter is medicated.
sections.dosage: 12 grams with lukewarm water, laghu trin panchmool kwath or warm milk.

fullContent:
Trikantaka Ghrita – Benefits, Usage, Indications and Dosage 
 Reference: Sahasrayogam Ghritaprakarana 
 Introduction 
 Trikantaka Ghrita is an Ayurvedic formulation with clarified butter as its base. It is basically used to cure urinary and renal disorders. 
 Ingredients 
 
 Trikantaka (Tribulus terrestris] 
 Water for decoction – 12.288 liters boiled and reduced to 3.072 liters 
 
 9.140 grams of each of:- 
 
 Cardamom (Elettaria cardamomum) 
 Shilajit (Asphaltum) 
 Shilabheda (Aerva lanata) 
 Licorice (Glycyrrhiza glabra) 
 Shatavari (Asparagus racemosus) 
 Darbha (Desmostachya bipinnata) 
 Ambu (Pavonia odorata) 
 Shaundi (Piper longum) 
 Vasuka (Adhatoda zeylanica) 
 Vasiraka (Piper cubeba) 
 Kasha (Saccharum spontaneum) 
 Ikshumoola (Root of sugarcane) 
 Matsyakshika (Enhydra fluctuans) 
 Milk 
 Ghee / Clarified butter 
 
 Method of Preparation 
 Combine the mentioned herbs and decoction and add them to the clarified butter. Heat them till the herbs are completely infused in it and the clarified butter is medicated. 
 Dosage 
 12 grams with lukewarm water, laghu trin panchmool kwath or warm milk. 
 Indications 
 
 Dysuria 
 Renal colic 
 Diabetes 
 Urinary disorders 
 
 Contraindications 
 
 There are no reported side effects with this medicine. 
 Self-medication should be avoided. 
 Over dosage might lead to diarrhea. 
 
 
 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.
